newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ wool prices improve at Christchurch sale.
newsitem.headline: NZ wool prices improve at Christchurch sale.

text.p: Wool prices improved at Thursday's sale in Christchurch, with the market indicator up 14 cents to 464 NZ cents per kg clean, Wools of New Zealand said.
The strong segment indicator rose 13 cents to 394, while the medium segment rose 34 to 601 cents.
Compared to the June 5 sale in Napier, prices for crossbred fleece of 35/36 micron were two to four percent dearer, while prices for 37 micron and stronger were flat to 2.5 percent dearer.
First lambs 75/100 mm and longer were 7.5 percent dearer, and 50/75 mm were 1.5 to three percent dearer.
Second lambs were unchanged, while bulky skirtings were 1.5 percent dearer. Second shear bellies and pieces and crutchings were three percent dearer.
Of the 2,362 clean tonnes on offer, 17 percent failed to meet growers price reserves.

The offer comprised 44 percent crossbred fleece, 13 percent second shear, 11 percent lambswool, eight percent crutchings, seven percent bulky skirtings, four percent second shear bellies and pieces and three percent halfbred fleece.
The balance was made up of miscellaneous wools.
New Zealand exporters said the main bidding came from China, Western Europe and India, with support from Pakistan, Australia, Turkey, Nepal and local mills.
The next sales will be at Christchurch and Napier on June 26.
